subject: general
question: In which of the following years was the monetary policy framework moved towards flexible inflation targeting and a six member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) constituted for setting the policy rate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2016**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The monetary policy framework was shifted towards **Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT)** in **2016** to maintain price stability and support economic growth.
 
• A **six-member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** was constituted in 2016 to decide the policy interest rates based on inflation targets set by the government.
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, was amended in 2016 to provide a statutory basis for a **monetary policy framework** centered on inflation targeting.
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and the Government of India signed an agreement in February 2015, which was operationalized in 2016 to implement the FIT framework.
 
• The inflation target was set at **4% with a tolerance band of ±2%**, aiming to keep inflation between 2% and 6%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT):**

 
 
• It is a monetary policy strategy where the central bank sets an inflation target and uses interest rates and other tools to achieve it.
 
• The goal is to maintain price stability while supporting overall economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):**
 
 
• The MPC is a statutory body constituted under the RBI Act, 1934, responsible for setting the policy repo rate to achieve inflation targets.
 
• It consists of six members: three from the RBI (including the Governor as the Chairperson) and three external members nominated by the Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Inflation Targeting Framework in India:**
 
 
• Adopted in 2016, it mandates the RBI to target inflation at 4% with a tolerance band of ±2%.
 
• The framework is reviewed every five years to reassess its effectiveness and make necessary adjustments.
 
 
 
• **Key Benefits of FIT:**
 
 
• Improves transparency and accountability in monetary policy decision-making.
 
• Helps anchor inflation expectations, leading to stable economic conditions.
 
• Reduces uncertainty in the economy, promoting investment and growth.
 
 
 
• **Challenges of FIT in India:**
 
 
• High dependency on supply-side factors like food and fuel prices, which are often volatile.
 
• Potential trade-off between inflation control and economic growth during periods of economic slowdown.
